messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content: No. Counterexample: B_n(x) = x^n. Each B_n is polynomial on [0,1]. Pointwise, B_n → f, where f(x) = 0 if x ∈ [0,1), f(1) = 1. Convergence fails uniformly: sup|B_n(x) − f(x)| = sup_{x<1} |x^n| = 1 for every n. Hence pointwise convergence does not guarantee uniform convergence, even polynomial sequences.
